ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two horizontal straight lines, the upper one labeled c, the lower one labeled d; two oblique straight lines a and b both slope from the lower left to the upper right. Angle 4 is located at the intersection of line b and the upper horizontal line c, and is on the upper right of the intersection; angle 2 is located at the intersection of line a and c, also on the upper right; angle 1 and angle 2 are both above line c, respectively located on the left side and right side of oblique line a. raw_record.question_text: In the figure, $a \parallel b, c \parallel d$, and $m\angle 4 = 57$. Find the measure of $\angle 1$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: line c is the upper horizontal line, and slanted parallel lines a and b intersect it. Angle 4 is at the intersection of b with c in the upper-right position; angle 2 is at the intersection of a with c in the corresponding upper-right position; angle 1 is adjacent to angle 2 above line c. From the text, a ∥ b and m∠4 = 57. Using c as a transversal of the parallel lines a and b, corresponding angles give ∠2 = ∠4 = 57. Then ∠1 and ∠2 form a linear pair on line c, so m∠1 = 180 - 57 = 123.
